newsitem.title: USA: Leasing Edge sees 1996 year loss.
newsitem.headline: Leasing Edge sees 1996 year loss.

text.p: Leasing Edge Corp said Thursday it expected to report a loss of up to $1.5 million despite an increase in revenues of up to $22 million for 1996.
The company said preliminary, unaudited figures showed revenues for the year totalling between $20 million and $22 million, about 16 percent higher than the previous year.

"However ...we anticipate a loss for 1996, resulting primarily from an adjustment to write inventories down to their net realizable value, inventory problems at our Pacific Mountain Computer subsidiary, and certain other writedowns," it said.
It said it foresaw reporting a loss between $1.0 million and $1.5 million for the year.

The company said it had solved its inventory problem at Pacific Mountain and implemented a plan to consolidate operations at Pacific Mountain with those of its newly acquired subsidiary, Superior Computer Systems.

Based in Las Vegas, Leasing Edge and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, Pacific Mountain and Superior Computer Systems lease, supply and distribute computer and telecommunications equipment to large corporations and institutions.
